basis.note: Since Nov 2026 the primary basis is the ACS inorganic content map (read in full); every articulation is answered (scripts/accm_maps.py), unit 15 holding the principles the chapter units did not reach. Units follow the chapters of Cotton & Wilkinson 6e (table of contents read); the objectives are a house list on those chapters.

big_ideas.title: Count electrons
big_ideas.text: Shapes, bond orders, cluster types and oxidation states all come from counting valence electrons and placing them.

big_ideas.title: Trends and their exceptions
big_ideas.text: Size, charge and electronegativity change steadily across and down the table; the first row and the heaviest elements are where the named exceptions live.

practices.title: Compute
practices.text: Carry an electron count, oxidation state or energy to a number.

practices.title: Recall
practices.text: Know the compound, the product, the structure.

practices.title: Predict
practices.text: Use a model (VSEPR, MO, Wade, HSAB) to say what a species does.

los.do: Classify acids and bases as hard, soft or borderline and predict which pairs bind.
ek: Hard prefers hard, soft prefers soft.

los.do: Combine Latimer-diagram steps through free energies.
ek: E = Σ nE / Σ n.

los.do: Decide from a Latimer diagram whether a species disproportionates.
ek: E_right > E_left: it disproportionates.

los.do: Classify a hydride as saline, molecular or metallic.
ek: s-block saline; p-block molecular; many d-block interstitial.

los.do: Predict the shift of a vibration on deuteration from reduced masses.
Give the product of burning an alkali metal, and the oxidation state in oxides, peroxides and superoxides.
ek: Li₂O, Na₂O₂, KO₂; O −2, −1, −½.

los.do: Rank the thermal stability of group 2 carbonates.
ek: Rises down the group as cations grow less polarising.

los.do: Use the diagonal relationship.
ek: Li–Mg, Be–Al, B–Si.

los.do: Classify a borane as closo, nido or arachno with Wade's rules.
ek: n+1, n+2, n+3 skeletal pairs.

los.do: Rank boron trihalide Lewis acidity and explain it by π donation.
ek: BF₃ < BCl₃ < BBr₃.

los.do: Use the inert-pair effect, and find average oxidation states in mixed-valence group 13 compounds.
ek: Tl(I), Pb(II), Bi(III); GaCl₂ = Ga⁺[GaCl₄]⁻.

los.do: Classify carbides and count fullerene rings.
ek: Acetylides, methanides, covalent, interstitial; 12 pentagons always.

los.do: Give bond orders of species isoelectronic with N₂.
ek: CO, CN⁻, NO⁺, C₂²⁻: 3.

los.do: Relate silicate structure to O:Si ratio, and predict group 14 shapes.
ek: O/Si = 4 − s/2; Sn(II) has a lone pair.

los.do: Give oxidation states of nitrogen across its oxides and hydrides, and bond orders of NO and its ions.
Give the basicity of phosphorus oxoacids.
ek: Only O–H is acidic: 1, 2, 3.

los.do: Predict shapes of group 15 halides and their ions.
ek: PCl₅ = [PCl₄]⁺[PCl₆]⁻.

los.do: Give bond orders and unpaired electrons of O₂ and its ions from MO theory.
ek: O₂ 2 with two unpaired; superoxide 1.5; peroxide 1.

los.do: Predict shapes of group 16 compounds and oxidation states in sulfur oxoanions.
ek: SF₄ seesaw; thiosulfate +2 average.

units.title: The halogens and the noble gases (ch. 13–14)

los.do: Predict interhalogen and polyhalide shapes.
ek: ClF₃ T-shaped, I₃⁻ linear, ICl₄⁻ square planar.

los.do: Give halogen oxidation states in oxoanions and rank oxoacid strength.
ek: +1 to +7; HClO₄ strongest.

los.do: Predict shapes and oxidation states of xenon compounds.
ek: XeF₂ linear, XeF₄ square planar; even states +2 to +8.

los.do: Describe group 12 behaviour: Hg₂²⁺, amphoteric ZnO, colourless d¹⁰ compounds, and their oxidation states.
ek: Hg(I) is a dimer; d¹⁰ has no d–d colour.

los.do: Find the d count and the number of unpaired electrons of a complex.
ek: dⁿ = group − oxidation state; fill t₂g/e_g by spin.

los.do: Compute spin-only moments and CFSE.
Use the spectrochemical series and predict Jahn–Teller distortions.
ek: I⁻ < … < CN⁻ < CO; uneven e_g distorts.

los.do: Predict whether a complex is labile or inert.
ek: d³ and low-spin d⁶ are inert.

los.do: Give the products of permanganate by pH and the chromate–dichromate equilibrium.
ek: Mn²⁺, MnO₂, MnO₄²⁻; acid orange, base yellow.

los.do: Give oxidation states in first-row oxides and oxo ions, including mixed valence.
ek: Fe₃O₄ +8/3; VO²⁺ V(IV).

los.do: Find metal–metal bond orders from d counts.
ek: σ²π⁴δ² is a quadruple bond.

los.do: Explain the lanthanide contraction, low spin in 4d/5d, and the trans effect.
ek: Zr ≈ Hf; heavy complexes low spin; cisplatin route.

units.title: Group 3, the lanthanides and the actinides (ch. 19–20)

los.do: Count f electrons in lanthanide and actinide ions.
ek: Ln³⁺ 4fⁿ, n = Z − 57.

los.do: Compute a lanthanide ion's magnetic moment from its ground term.
Give characteristic oxidation states of lanthanides and actinides, and states in actinyl ions.
ek: Ce⁴⁺, Eu²⁺; U +6 as UO₂²⁺.

los.do: Count valence electrons in organometallic complexes.
ek: 18 for carbonyls; 16 for square-planar d⁸.

los.do: Follow electron count and oxidation state through oxidative addition and the other elementary steps.
ek: OA: +2 ox, +2 CN, +2 e.

los.do: Name the catalyst of the major industrial homogeneous processes and track electron counts round a cycle.
ek: Monsanto, Wacker, Ziegler–Natta, Wilkinson, oxo, metathesis; 16/18 alternation.

units.title: Inorganic principles across the ACS content map

los.do: Estimate the effective nuclear charge on a valence electron with Slater's rules.
ek: S = 0.35 per other electron in the same (ns, np) group, 0.85 per electron in shell n − 1, 1.00 per electron deeper; for an ns electron of a d-block atom the (n − 1)d electrons count 0.85.

los.do: Decide from a molecule's point group whether it can be polar and whether it can be chiral.
ek: Polar only in C₁, Cₛ, Cₙ and Cₙᵥ; chiral only when there is no improper axis (C₁, Cₙ, Dₙ).

los.do: Find an organometallic fragment's isolobal organic partner from its electron count.
ek: A fragment one electron short of 18 (Mn(CO)₅, CpFe(CO)₂) is isolobal with CH₃ (one short of 8); two short with CH₂; three short with CH.

los.do: Compare ligands by steric bulk (cone angle) and by donor or acceptor strength.
ek: Tolman cone angle grows PMe₃ < PPh₃ < PCy₃ < P(t-Bu)₃; stronger π-acceptors (CO, PF₃, phosphites) raise the ν(CO) of the other carbonyls.

los.do: Identify constitutional isomers of complexes and use precipitation or conductivity to tell them apart.
ek: Ionisation, hydrate, linkage and coordination isomers; only ions outside the coordination sphere precipitate with Ag⁺ or Ba²⁺ (Werner's evidence).

los.do: Name a coordination compound and write the formula from a name.
ek: Ligands alphabetically before the metal; anionic ligands end in -o; the metal takes -ate in an anionic complex, with its oxidation state in Roman numerals.

los.do: Find a lattice enthalpy or an enthalpy of formation from a Born–Haber cycle.
ek: ΔH_f = ΔH_sub + IE + ½D + ΔH_eg + ΔH_lattice (lattice formation from gaseous ions, negative).

los.do: Relate point defects and nonstoichiometry to composition and oxidation state.
ek: Schottky: cation–anion vacancy pairs; Frenkel: an ion moved to an interstitial site; in Fe₁₋ₓO each missing Fe²⁺ is balanced by two Fe³⁺.

los.do: Classify doped semiconductors and predict how conductivity changes with temperature.
ek: Group 15 dopants in Si give n-type, group 13 p-type; intrinsic carriers grow as e^(−E_g/2kT), so semiconductors conduct better when hot while metals conduct worse.

los.do: Recall superconductors, perovskites, polymorphs, layered solids and crystal systems.
ek: Below T_c resistance vanishes and fields are expelled (Meissner); Cooper pairs (BCS) in conventional ones; YBa₂Cu₃O₇ is a layered perovskite; 7 crystal systems, 14 Bravais lattices, 230 space groups.

los.do: Describe framework, self-assembled and nanoscale materials and how synthesis sets their properties.
ek: MOFs join metal nodes with organic linkers into porous crystals; thiols on gold self-assemble into monolayers; quantum dots' band gaps widen as they shrink.

los.do: Assign a substitution mechanism (A, D, Iₐ, I_d) and compute a rate through an outer-sphere pre-equilibrium.
ek: Eigen–Wilkins: k_obs = K_os k_i [L]; a negative volume of activation and dependence on the entering ligand point to association; square-planar d⁸ is associative.

los.do: Tell inner- from outer-sphere electron transfer and estimate a cross rate with the Marcus relation.
ek: Inner sphere needs a bridging ligand that is transferred (Taube: Cl from Co to Cr); outer sphere keeps both coordination shells; k₁₂ ≈ √(k₁₁k₂₂K₁₂).

los.do: Use the trans effect to plan the synthesis of a square-planar isomer.
ek: Trans effect order roughly CO, CN⁻ > PR₃ > I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > NH₃ > H₂O; [PtCl₄]²⁻ + 2 NH₃ gives cis-platin, [Pt(NH₃)₄]²⁺ + 2 Cl⁻ gives the trans isomer.

los.do: Quantify the chelate effect and explain its entropic and kinetic origins.
ek: Chelates release more free ligands (entropy gain) and, once one end binds, the other is held near the metal; ΔΔG = −RT ln 10 · Δlog β.

los.do: Compute the barrier of a fluxional process from NMR coalescence.
ek: At coalescence k = πΔν/√2; ΔG‡ = RT ln(k_B T/(h k)); Berry pseudorotation exchanges axial and equatorial sites of a trigonal bipyramid.

los.do: Combine stepwise formation constants and find the fraction of each complex at a given ligand concentration.
ek: β_n = K₁K₂…K_n; α_ML = β₁[L]/(1 + β₁[L] + β₂[L]² + …); Irving–Williams: Mn < Fe < Co < Ni < Cu > Zn.

los.do: Predict acid–base behaviour in nonaqueous solvents, levelling and superacids.
ek: The strongest acid that can exist in a solvent is its lyonium ion; acids stronger than that are levelled; differentiating solvents (acetic acid) separate them; superacids have H₀ below −12.

los.do: Relate a chiral catalyst's selectivity to the free-energy difference of the competing transition states.
ek: er = e^(ΔΔG‡/RT), ee = (er − 1)/(er + 1); about 11 kJ/mol at 25 °C gives 98% ee.

los.do: Use LFSE to explain the double hump in hydration enthalpies of first-row M²⁺ ions.
ek: High-spin octahedral LFSE (in Δ_o): 0, −0.4, −0.8, −1.2, −0.6, 0, −0.4, −0.8, −1.2, −0.6, 0 for d⁰–d¹⁰; d⁰, d⁵ and d¹⁰ lie on the baseline.

los.do: Find Δ_o from a d–d absorption and apply the selection rules and Tanabe–Sugano reading of d–d spectra.
ek: For d¹, Δ_o = hc/λ_max (ν̃ = 10⁷/λ in cm⁻¹); Laporte-forbidden d–d bands are weak, spin-forbidden ones weaker; Tanabe–Sugano diagrams map band energies to Δ_o/B.

los.do: Compute an effective magnetic moment from a measured susceptibility and infer the number of unpaired electrons.
ek: μ_eff = 2.828 √(χ_M T) (cgs) ≈ √(8χ_M T); spin-only μ = √(n(n + 2)).

los.do: Predict multiplets in multinuclear NMR from spin I and the number of equivalent coupled nuclei.
ek: Lines = 2nI + 1: three ¹⁹F split ³¹P into a 1:3:3:1 quartet; deuterium (I = 1) splits ¹³C of CDCl₃ into a 1:1:1 triplet.

los.do: Use an ion-selective electrode's Nernstian response, and choose a microscopy or luminescence technique.
ek: ΔE = (RT ln 10/zF)·Δlog a, 59.16/z mV per decade at 25 °C; fluorescence is spin-allowed and fast (ns), phosphorescence spin-forbidden and slow; STM and AFM reach atoms.

los.do: Choose the technique and precautions for air-sensitive, pressurised and cryogenic work.
ek: Schlenk line or glovebox under N₂ or Ar; never seal a cryogen in a closed vessel; liquid N₂ can condense O₂; check pressure ratings and use blast shields.
